card.name: Gombhira
card.era: Traditional (post-7th/8th c.; modern form ~150 years old)
card.tagline: Malda's satirical Shiva folk-theatre of dance and song
card.profile: Gombhira (also Gambhira/Gamvira) is a traditional Bengali folk performing art of the Malda district of West Bengal, combining musical theatre, dance, song and satire to address social and regional issues, typically performed by all-male troupes during Shiva-worshipping festivals (Wikipedia; MAP Academy). Its name derives from 'gombhir' (poise/gravity), a quality associated with Shiva; performances traditionally took place between April and June as part of Chaitra Sankranti / Gajan celebrations (MAP Academy). A typical performance unfolds in stages - bandana (invocation to Shiva), dwaita (duet), charyaari, palabandi gaan (provocation) and khabar (reporting) - and in its classic form two performers, one representing Shiva, converse about everyday hardships (Indian Culture portal).
card.insight: Gombhira evolved from the song-and-dance forms of the Koch people of the Malda region and is tied to local mango cultivation and Shiva worship; it survives in Malda and Murshidabad in India and in Dinajpur, Rangpur and Rajshahi in Bangladesh, where grandfather-and-grandson figures critique sociopolitical issues (MAP Academy; Wikipedia).
